newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mining giant RTZ-CRA sees profits fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mining giant RTZ-CRA sees profits fall.

text.p: The world's biggest mining company RTZ-CRA on Thursday reported a 24 percent drop in 1996 profits, but soothed investors' sentiment with upbeat comments over its near-term prospects.
Net profit after tax fell to $1.096 billion in 1996 from $1.441 billion in 1995 following sharply lower metal prices and operational problems with its U.S. Kennecott copper smelter.
Adverse exchange rates were an additional factor behind the fall, which was widely expected.
If anything, industry watchers took heart from upbeat comments from RTZ-CRA, which said it that higher production volumes and a lower effective tax rate would underpin its 1997 performance.
"I expect our growth to continue at a rate in advance of the market overall," RTZ chairman Robert Wilson said.

RTZ-CRA, formed through a merger late in 1995, also announced that it plans to change its name to Rio Tinto, to help create a clear identity. "It is highly desirable to have a single identity rather than the confusing image stemming from the double acronym," Wilson said.
Anglo-Australian RTZ-CRA suffered from a 22 percent drop in copper prices in 1996 and a 16 percent fall in aluminium in the wake of the trading scandal triggered by Sumitomo trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
But prices have picked up in recent months and Wilson said he expected conditions in the copper market to remain tight in the short term.
"We do expect the tightness is going to ease, maybe not this year, but perhaps as we go into 1998," Wilson said.
The price drop last year depressed profits by $311 million, while technical hitches at the flagship Kennecott smelter in Utah cost the mining giant about $150 million.
Adverse currency movements shaved another $38 million off the 1996 results.
RTZ-CRA, sees strong long-term growth in demand for metals and minerals and expects its smelter problems to be solved by June following final repair works, which are scheduled to start in April.

"The resolution of the problems at Kennecott and what we're seeing at the moment in the aluminium and copper prices will see them (RTZ-CRA) post a fairly strong recovery," said analyst Emile Morfett at Paribas Capital Markets. He said RTZ-CRA will benefit this year from the first full year of production at the Greens Creek silver, zinc and copper mine in the United States.
Expansion of the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand and increased operations at the huge Escondida copper mine in Chile will also have a positive impact.
Wilson said RTZ-CRA's capital expenditure will likely hover around an annual $1.5 billion in the next three years after spending $1.75 billion last year.
Shares in RTZ were barely changed in London, trading 1/2 a penny lower at 943-1/2 in mid-morning business after the Sydney market, where CRA is listed, had already closed.
